This digital, interactive textbook contains the lecture and practicals for the Python class. It is intended to be a one-stop-shop where you can access all of the educational materials we’ll be using.

Attention

This textbook is under construction and may change (very) often!

In this lecture, you will first find the basics of Python programming, and then we will go throught chemistry oriented problem. The lecture will essentially be based on Active Learning, meaning that you will be actively involved and doing something besides passively listening. In particular, you will have to read many things by yourselves, and you will have the occasion to verify your understanding all along the way with small exercices.

You can use the navigation panel on the left to jump quickly between sections of this textbook, even though it is intended to be read in the order of the sections. You can also use the navigation panel on the right to jump between the sub-sections of a given section.
You will have to complete many exercices, generally using what we call a Jupyter Notebook. To do so, you will be able to download the notebooks directly from this textbook by clicking on the Download icon at the top right of the page ; you will then work on these notebooks on yous own computer

Python is a high-level programming language released in 1991 by Guido van Rossum, and since then it has become one of the most popular programming languages in the world. In particular, it is really popular among scientists, and it is also often teached as the first contact with programming. Indeed, Python is interesting for several reasons:

Open-source, i.e. free, works on all major OS (Windows, Mac, Linux...)

Clear and simple syntax that looks close to natural language

Huge amount of libraries that extend the functionnalities of Python, in particular for sciences

Great documentation and forum

Python comes in different distributions, which are packaged versions of Python that include the interpreter (what reads and executes the program) along with additional libraries and tools. They are designed for specific use cases, such as Anaconda for data science, CPython as the standard reference implementation, and PyPy for improved performance. These distributions make Python easier to install and use for different needs. For this lecture, we are going to use Miniconda, which stands for Minimalist Anaconda.

Go to the Anaconda download page: 

Anaconda download

Scroll down to the page bottom, it will look like the following picture, and click on “Download Miniconda Installer”



On the next page, select and download the installer corresponding to Miniconda, see figure below



When the download is done, open the file and install Miniconda with all the default parameters (you can install the software for your session only if you haven’t admin rights on the computer you are using).

If the installation ran smoothly, a new application called Anaconda Prompt should be available on your Windows session. To find it, just type *Ana
In general, it is a good practice to create what is called a Python environment
